latin.583: §. XVIII. A Waldensibus kat' exochēn sic dictis, i.e. in Gallia Seculo XII. natis, & XIII. propagatis, originem traxere WALDENSES ANGLI, SECULO XIV, unô nomine WICLEPHISTÆ dicti à Johanne Wiclepho, Doctore Anglo, qui floruit Anno 1370. Hujus Theses, tum Transsubstantiationi, tum Consubstantiationi oppositas, partim ex Concilio Constantiensi, in quo damnatæ sunt, partim ex IV. libro Trialog. cap. 7. & 43. de Sermone Domini in monte, collegit Franciscus Foris Otrokocsi in Irenico p. 57. & 58.
latin.584: TRANSSUBSTANTIATIONI ita contradicit Wicleph: Substantia panis manet in altari post Consecrationem & non definit esse panis. Item: Hostia consecrata, est naturaliter verus panis, & sacramentaliter corpus Christi. Item: Sicut Christus est simul Deus & homo, ita hostia consecrata est simul corpus Christi & verus panis: Quia est corpus Domini IN FIGURA, & verus panis IN NATURA.
latin.585: Item: Sicut Johannes Baptista figuraliter fuit Elias, & non personaliter, ita panis in altari FIGURALITER est corpus Christi, & absque omni ambiguitate hæc est FIGURATA locutio, sicut illa: Johannes ipse est Elias.
latin.586: Et infra: Nec audiendi sunt Heretici qui sensum istum nituntur excludere, per hoc falsum: quod Evangelium nec ante, nec post, habet talem modum loquendi figurativum; Nam Lucæ 22. statim subjungitur: Hoc facite in meam commemorationem. Acsi diceretur: Hic panis sacramentalis inefficacem mei memoriam capi debet, cum mens Catholici non capiat, quod panis sit corpus Christi nisi intelligendo FIGURATIVE.
latin.587: CONSUBSTANTIATIONEM autem hisce refutat: Sum certus, inquit, quod sententia Impanationis est impossibilis atque hæreticæ, quia sic corpus Christi nedum foret factum à Presbytero celebrante, sed & à pistore; & generaliter Sacerdos celebrans, collum & omnia membra Christi frangeret.
latin.588: Idem alibi, libro de Eucharistia cap. 4. Sanctus (inquit) Ambrosius non intendit dicere, quòd panis fiat identicè corpus Christi, sed quod fiat ejus FIGURA EFFICAX. Observa, FIGURAM EFFICACEM Wiclephum in Cœna statuere, quâ ratione & verba institutionis figuratè intelligenda, & præsentiam interim corporis Christi realissimam, à qua omnis Eucharistiæ efficacitas promanat, in S. Eucharistia omninò admittendam esse, contendit.

pass_a.583: §. XVIII. From the Waldenses so called kat' exochēn — i.e. born in Gaul in the XIIth Age and propagated in the XIIIth — the ENGLISH WALDENSES drew their origin in the XIVth AGE, called by one name Wycliffites from John Wycliffe, English Doctor, who flourished in the Year 1370. His Theses opposed both to Transubstantiation and to Consubstantiation Franciscus Foris Otrokocsi collected in the Irenicum pp. 57 and 58, partly from the Council of Constance in which they were condemned, partly from Book IV of the Trialog chapters 7 and 43 On the Lord’s Sermon on the Mount.
pass_a.584: Wycliffe thus contradicts TRANSUBSTANTIATION: The substance of bread remains on the altar after Consecration and does not cease to be bread. Likewise: The consecrated Host is naturally true bread, and sacramentally the body of Christ. Likewise: As Christ is at once God and man, so the consecrated host is at once the body of Christ and true bread: Because it is the Lord’s body IN FIGURE, and true bread IN NATURE.
pass_a.585: Likewise: As John the Baptist was figurally Elijah, and not personally, so the bread on the altar is FIGURALLY the body of Christ, and without any ambiguity this is FIGURATIVE speech, as that: John himself is Elijah.
pass_a.586: And below: Nor are Heretics to be heard who strive to shut out that sense by this falsehood — that the Gospel neither before nor after has such a figurative mode of speaking; For in Luke 22 there is immediately subjoined: Do this in remembrance of me. As if it were said: This sacramental bread ought to be taken as an efficacious memory of me, since the Catholic mind does not grasp that bread is Christ’s body except by understanding FIGURATIVELY.
pass_a.587: But CONSUBSTANTIATION he refutes by these: I am certain, he says, that the sentence of Impanation is impossible and heretical, because thus Christ’s body would be made not only by the celebrating Presbyter but also by the baker; and generally the celebrating Priest would break Christ’s neck and all His members.
pass_a.588: The same elsewhere, in the book On the Eucharist ch. 4: Holy Ambrose (he says) does not intend to say that the bread becomes identically Christ’s body, but that it becomes His EFFICACIOUS FIGURE. Observe that Wycliffe sets an EFFICACIOUS FIGURE in the Supper, by which reason he contends both that the Institution words are to be understood figuratively and that meanwhile the most real presence of Christ’s body — from which all the Eucharist’s efficacy flows — is altogether to be admitted in the Sacred Eucharist.

583: §.XVIII: from the Waldenses so called par excellence — born in Gaul in Age XII, spread in XIII — came the ENGLISH WALDENSES of Age XIV.
One name: Wycliffites, from John Wycliffe (English doctor, ~1370). Otrokocsi gathers his theses against both Transubstantiation and Consubstantiation from Constance (where condemned) and the Trialog.
584: Wycliffe against Transubstantiation: after consecration the bread’s substance remains on the altar — it does not cease to be bread.
The consecrated Host is naturally true bread and sacramentally Christ’s body — at once body and true bread, as Christ is at once God and man: the Lord’s body IN FIGURE, true bread IN NATURE.
585: As John the Baptist was figurally Elijah, not personally, so the altar bread is FIGURALLY Christ’s body.
Without ambiguity this is FIGURATIVE speech — like ‘John himself is Elijah.’
586: Heretics who deny any figurative Gospel speech are not to be heard — Luke 22 at once adds ‘Do this in remembrance of me.’
As if: this sacramental bread is for efficacious memory of me; the Catholic mind grasps bread as Christ’s body only by understanding FIGURATIVELY.
587: Against Consubstantiation / Impanation Wycliffe is certain: the sentence is impossible and heretical.
Otherwise Christ’s body would be made not only by the celebrating priest but by the baker — and the celebrant would break Christ’s neck and all His members.
588: On the Eucharist ch. 4: Ambrose does not mean bread becomes identically Christ’s body, but His EFFICACIOUS FIGURE.
So Wycliffe holds both: Institution words figurative, and the most real presence of Christ’s body — source of all Eucharistic efficacy — fully admitted. Stop before §.XIX.
